method: Permute whole draw rows, preserving each draw's six-number structure and full-history per-number totals; compare first-half and second-half frequency vectors.
conclusion: No evidence of positive persistent number-frequency bias in this chronological split. The observed correlation is negative; the upper-tail permutation probability for positive persistence is 0.9472.
limitations: Exploratory split chosen from available history, not preregistered.
One test only; does not establish absence of all possible biases.
Not a prospective validation and not strict PASS.
Cannot be used to claim a predictive model.
